newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks edge up led by domestic buyers.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks edge up led by domestic buyers.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly up on Monday supported by local investors, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.68 points up at 637.54. Price declines edged out gains by 29 to 26. Lanka Orix Leasing Co rose 2.50 to 157, Sathosa Motors four to 55. National Development Bank Ltd fell two rupees to 196, Serendib Hotels Ltd 3.50 3.50 to 12.50.
"Local investors dominated with many foreigners on Easter holiday," said Seedantha Kulatilkeke of Allied Phillips.
Despite active buying, profit-taking by investors starved of incomes for over six months was restraining the index, he said.
Turnover was 30.9 million rupees on one million shares, led by 54,000 CF Ventures, 14,100 Development Finance, 30,000 Grain Elevators, 18,000 Haycarb, 34,000 Kotagala Plantations.
"The depth of the market is improving as investors focus on a wider range of shares," Kulatilleke said.
Investors believe that conditions conducive to good corporate growth in 1997 such as low cost borrowings will have a positive impact on many shares, brokers said.
The Central Bank cut reserve ratios by two percentage points to 12 last week to improve money supply and lower cost of company borrowings, which investors see as a favourable step.
